observation_summary: The LocaleUtils.toLocale method failed to parse locale strings starting with an underscore, which is a valid format according to Locale.toString() documentation.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves implementing a new branch of logic to handle the specific case where a locale string starts with an underscore. This is a procedural correction to the parsing algorithm, as the existing method only accounted for standard language-first formats. It is not a simple guard (Checking) or a value assignment (Assignment/Initialization), but a structural expansion of the parsing logic to support a missing case.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'LocaleUtils.toLocale does not parse strings starting with an underscore'
The fix diff adds a new conditional block (if (ch0 == '_')) to handle this specific format, which was previously missing from the parsing algorithm.
The stack trace shows an IllegalArgumentException being thrown for '_GB', which is a valid locale format that the original code did not account for.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds checks, the primary issue is the absence of the logic required to parse the underscore-prefixed format, not just a missing validation of an existing format.
This is a local procedural correction within an existing method, not a design-level capability gap.
